user.title: Connect to an SSH relay
user.description: Home Assistant opens a reverse SSH tunnel to the relay VM as user `relay-<tenant>`, authenticated with a key generated on the next step. No password is used.

data_description.relay_host: IP address or hostname of the relay VM.
data_description.tenant: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, up to 24 characters. Same name as in the relay's tenants file.
data_description.remote_port: Port reserved for this tenant on the relay (18000-18999).
data_description.local_host: Where the relay traffic goes. Usually `homeassistant` on Home Assistant OS.

key.title: Add the key to the relay
key.description:
Add this tenant to the relay's tenants file, then run `relay-setup.sh` on the relay. Replace the domain with the name you reach Home Assistant at.

```
{tenant_snippet}
```

Public key:

```
{public_key}
```

Submit to test the connection. The relay host key seen now is then pinned.

key_failed.title: Connection test failed
key_failed.description:
{reason}

Tenant entry for the relay:

```
{tenant_snippet}
```

Public key: `{public_key}`

Test again, or save anyway: the tunnel then waits for the relay to know the key and pins the host key on the first connection.

error.invalid_tenant: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes only, 1 to 24 characters.
error.invalid_auth: The relay rejected the key: it is not on the relay yet. Add the tenant and run relay-setup.sh.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the relay. Check the host, the SSH port and the network.
error.forward_refused: The relay refused the port forward: the port is not the one of this tenant, or another tenant uses it.
error.host_key_mismatch: The relay presented a host key other than the expected one.

abort.already_configured: This tenant of this relay is already configured.

data_description.remote_port: Must match the port of this tenant on the relay (18000-18999).

regenerate_key.title: New client key
regenerate_key.description:
Replace the public key of this tenant on the relay, then run `relay-setup.sh`. Until then the relay rejects the tunnel. The relay host key stays pinned.

```
{tenant_snippet}
```

Public key:

```
{public_key}
```

Submit to save the new key.

forget_host_key.title: Forget the relay host key
forget_host_key.description: The next connection accepts the host key the relay presents and pins it. Only do this if you know why the relay host key changed (relay reinstalled).

host_key_changed.title: The SSH relay host key changed

confirm.title: Accept the new relay host key?
confirm.description:
The relay {host} presented the host key {actual}, but {expected} is pinned. The tunnel stays closed.

If you reinstalled the relay, accept: the next connection pins the new key. Otherwise, someone may be impersonating the relay: do not accept.
